name: Vor's Prize
prereq: None — starts on your first login.
rewards: Ship segments (Arsenal, Mods, Foundry, Market access), Ascaris Negator, starter gear
story: You wake from cryosleep with the Lotus as your guide and Captain Vor of the Grineer hunting you. The tutorial quest that teaches movement, modding, and mission types while establishing the core conflict: the Tenno are back, and everyone wants them dead.
tips: Solo tutorial. Take your time learning bullet-jumping and modding here — everything else builds on it.

name: Once Awake
prereq: Complete the Mercury Junction on Venus.
rewards: Heat Sword blueprint; introduces the Corpus faction
story: A Corpus researcher offers a cure for the Infestation in exchange for your help. First real look at the Corpus and the Infested as factions — and your first crafted melee weapon.
tips: Solo. A short quest; craft the Heat Sword when you can, it's a fine early melee.

name: The Archwing
prereq: Complete the Mars Junction on Earth.
rewards: Odonata Archwing, Imperator (arch-gun), Veritux (arch-melee), Archwing Launcher segment
story: Corpus ships are bombarding from orbit and you need wings to reach them. Unlocks Archwings — the space-flight system required for parts of the star chart, Railjack-adjacent content, and later open-world skies.
tips: Solo. Archwing missions feel clunky at first; the launcher segment lets you deploy your Archwing in open worlds later, which is the real prize.

name: Stolen Dreams
prereq: Complete the Phobos Junction on Mars.
rewards: Access to Maroo's Bazaar and Ayatan Treasure Hunts
story: A thief named Maroo steals from the Grineer and drags you into her mess. Introduces Maroo's Bazaar (an early trading hub) and Ayatan sculptures — the treasure-hunt side economy that funds your mod upgrades via Endo.
tips: Solo. Start running Maroo's weekly Ayatan hunt once unlocked — it's the most reliable early Endo source.

name: The New Strange
prereq: Europa Junction + join Cephalon Simaris's Sanctuary syndicate and speak with him.
story: Simaris sends you hunting strange, merged Warframe-like beings across the system. The trail leads to Chroma — a frame literally made of other frames' parts — and the mystery of what the Sentients did to it. Unlocks Simaris standing and the Simulacrum testing room.
tips: Solo. The final fight is a gear check for new players — bring your best damage and don't be shy about reviving.

name: Natah
rewards: Story unlock — opens The Second Dream
story: A strange drone scans you and the Lotus reacts with something like fear. This is where the story stops being a shooter backdrop: the Sentients are real, Hunhow is awake, and the Lotus is hiding something enormous about who — and what — you are.
tips: Solo. Short and mostly story; play it when you're ready for the tone to change completely.

name: The Second Dream
rewards: The Operator; Focus schools; Somatic Link; Broken-War blueprint
story: The quest that redefined Warframe. The truth about the Tenno, the Zariman, and the Lotus comes out all at once — and you gain your Operator, a second playable form with Void powers, plus the Focus system that powers them up.
tips: Solo, and go in blind if you can — this is the story moment veterans still talk about. Have tissues and an hour free.

name: The War Within
rewards: Sorties (daily endgame missions); Riven mods; Kuva; Operator combat mode
story: The Grineer Queens want your body and Teshin pays the price for defying them. A brutal trial through the Kuva Fortress that forges your Operator into a fighter — and unlocks the entire endgame loop: Sorties, Rivens, and Kuva farming. Required before you can spawn a Kuva Lich.
tips: Solo. Longer than most quests; stock up and don't rush the fortress sections.

name: Chains of Harrow
prereq: Complete The War Within + complete the Mot Survival node in the Void.
story: A Red Veil operative's Warframe is possessed by something from the Void, and the Steel Meridian needs you to put it down. A horror-tinged story about faith, sacrifice, and what the Void does to people — and your path to building Harrow.
tips: Solo. Atmospheric and creepy; headphones recommended.

name: Apostasy Prologue
prereq: Complete Chains of Harrow + build the Personal Quarters segment.
story: Short, devastating, and best experienced unspoiled. The Lotus makes her choice, and everything you thought you knew about her breaks. Play it right before The Sacrifice.
tips: Solo. Very short — do it back-to-back with The Sacrifice for the full gut punch.

name: The Sacrifice
story: You hunt the truth about the Warframes' creation through the memories of a broken Dax soldier. The origin of the frames is darker than anyone admitted — and at the end, Umbra himself chooses to stand with you. Awards one of the most beloved frames in the game.
tips: Solo. Bring your best Operator gear for the later sections; the final fight rewards patience.

name: Prelude to War
story: A three-part build-up (Chimera Prologue, Erra, The Maker) as the Sentients return in force and old enemies make new bargains. The Paracesis you forge here is your answer to what's coming — and you'll want it maxed for the war ahead.
tips: Solo. Forge the Paracesis and rank it up; it's genuinely useful in the finale.

name: The New War
prereq: Complete Prelude to War + own a Railjack + own a Necramech.
rewards: Nataruk bow; unlocks the Zariman/Chrysalith; playable Drifter; Operator/Drifter swap
story: The Sentients invade the Origin System and you lose — everything. Told across three perspectives (including long stretches as Kahl, Veso, and Teshin), it's Warframe's Endgame-style crossover event, ending with the system changed forever and the Zariman opened.
tips: Mostly solo with some squad-friendly sections. It's long (several hours) — clear your evening. Build that Necramech and Railjack first or you're gated.

name: Angels of the Zariman
rewards: Chrysalith (Zariman hub) + Holdfasts syndicate; Incarnon weapons; Voidplume farming; Gyre parts via bounties
story: You return to the Zariman Ten Zero, the colony ship where the Tenno were made. Its halls are haunted by Void Angels and the Holdfasts — the adults who stayed behind. Establishes the Zariman as an endgame hub with some of the best weapon upgrades (Incarnons) in the game.
tips: Solo quest, then squad-friendly Zariman missions. Start working Holdfasts standing early — Incarnon adapters are worth it.

name: The Duviri Paradox
rewards: Duviri (open world); The Circuit; Incarnon Genesis adapters; Kullervo via Duviri content
story: You wake as the Drifter in an endless storybook loop ruled by a tyrant king's moods. A complete genre shift — roguelike runs, a color-shifting world tied to the king's emotions, and the answer to what happened to the Drifter who never made the deal.
tips: Playable solo or in squads. The Circuit is the fastest Incarnon adapter farm in the game — run it weekly.

name: Whispers in the Walls
rewards: Sanctum Anatomica (Albrecht's Laboratories) + Cavia syndicate; Arcane Dissolution; Qorvex and Dante parts
story: Albrecht Entrati's lab calls from beneath Deimos, and something down there has been whispering back. The Man in the Wall steps out of the shadows and into the plot — the saga's true antagonist finally takes the stage.
tips: Solo quest, then squad-friendly lab missions. The Cavia's Arcane Dissolution lets you break down unwanted arcanes — huge quality of life.

name: The Lotus Eaters
story: A short, strange interlude: a familiar signal from a 1999 that shouldn't exist. Sets the table for The Hex — don't skip the weirdness.
tips: Solo and brief. Play it right before The Hex.

name: The Hex
rewards: Höllvania (1999); Atomicycle; The Hex syndicate; Cyte-09 parts
story: 1999. A doomed mall in Höllvania, a protoframe resistance cell called The Hex, and Albrecht Entrati's time gambit collapsing around them. Warframe's boldest setting swing — Y2K aesthetics, a drivable Atomicycle, and a full romanceable ally system.
tips: Solo quest, then squad-friendly Höllvania. The Atomicycle is pure joy — do the KIM chats, they're genuinely well written.

name: Jade Shadows
rewards: Jade Warframe (parts from the Ascension mission on Uranus)
story: The Stalker returns — not as a boss, but as a man with something to protect. A tragic, quiet story about the last thing he has left, ending with Jade, a Warframe built around angelic support and the Jade Light.
tips: Solo. Then farm the Ascension mission on Brutus, Uranus for her parts — it's also a great Endo and arcanes farm.
